subject: FinServe production latency spike and cross-region failover
messages:
From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@finserve.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: VP Engineering <vp_engineering@finserve.com>, ops@finserve.com
Date: 2026-03-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

Markus / Redwood team,

We’re seeing a sharp increase in 5xx error rates and tail latency for the Payments API served out of eu-west-2 starting ~07:50 UTC. Error rate jumped to ~12% and P95 latency climbed from ~220ms to ~1.6s. This is directly impacting checkout conversions — we’ve had three failed batches in the last 10 minutes.

Attached is a metrics snapshot and a short Grafana link (internal). Please escalate — we need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for a fix.

Attachments: finserve_metrics_snapshot.png (PNG, 240KB)

Thanks,
Sam Wright
Ops Lead, FinServe
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@finserve.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, VP Engineering <vp_engineering@finserve.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the snapshot. I’m looped in with SE and SRE to triage now. Quick confirmation questions so we prioritize correctly:
- Is traffic primarily from EU customers or a global mix?
- Are there steady spikes in QPS or any recent deployment in your environment?

Immediate plan: Evelyn/Sean, can we run a partial cross-region traffic shift to eu-west-1 for a small percentage (10–20%) and validate error rate change? If that looks good we’ll increase the shift while watching session affinity. I’ll coordinate comms and keep VP Eng updated.

Markus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Sam Wright <sam.wright@finserve.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

Sam / Markus — initial triage:
- Observed CPU and GPU utilization on the serving fleet in eu-west-2 spike concurrent with increased QPS; SSD IO and network for a subset of worker nodes show elevated retransmits.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~15% which explains higher token compute per request and the latency increase.

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) Trigger controlled traffic shift to eu-west-1 for 15% of routed requests (can be path-based for Payments).
2) Increase per-instance concurrency cap temporarily to absorb bursts.
3) Enable prefix cache warmup for active prefixes from FinServe (we can prefetch top 200 prompts).

I’ve uploaded our failover runbook and step checklist: runbook_failover_steps.pdf. Sean — please coordinate the shift and post metrics after 5 and 15 minutes.

Evelyn
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Sam Wright <sam.wright@finserve.com>
Cc: vp_engineering@finserve.com
Date: 2026-03-29T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

All — executing controlled failover now per Evelyn’s checklist. Actions taken:
- Shifted 15% of Payments traffic to eu-west-1 via routing policy (canary key + path filter) at 08:57 UTC.
- Increased concurrency cap on eu-west-2 node pool by +20% and primed cache for hot prefixes.

Initial impact after 5 minutes: overall 5xx dropped from ~12% to ~5%; P95 latency for shifted traffic is ~240ms. However, we observed session-affinity mismatches for long-lived streams — a small subset experienced transient errors during rebind. Rolling back affinity timeout to reduce session loss.

I’ve filed INC-4721 to track the session-affinity regression and attached timelines and raw logs here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4721. Will post consolidated metrics at 09:20 UTC.

Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: VP Engineering <vp_engineering@finserve.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

Thanks for the update. We appreciate the quick mitigation but this incident caused measurable revenue loss for our EU region. We need:
1) A clear timeline of events and root cause hypothesis.
2) Proposed permanent mitigations and a date for when these will be implemented.
3) Compensation/credit discussion per our SLA — please have legal/sales advise.

Copying Laura from Redwood to expedite commercial discussion. I’d like an executive summary and RCA today if possible.

— VP Eng, FinServe
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: VP Engineering <vp_engineering@finserve.com>, Sam Wright <sam.wright@finserve.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike eu-west-2 — impacting transactions

VP Eng / Sam — thank you and apologies for the disruption. Executive summary and immediate next steps:

Summary:
- Timeline: 07:50 UTC — error rate and P95 latency climb in eu-west-2. 08:57 UTC — 15% traffic shift to eu-west-1 initiated; 09:02 UTC — error rate reduced to ~3–5% overall.
- Root cause (preliminary): localized serving node network retransmits + reduced KV cache hit rate after a short burst of high QPS; this combined to increase compute per request and push nodes past optimal tail-latency operating point.

Immediate remedial actions we executed:
- Controlled cross-region traffic shift (canary) to eu-west-1.
- Temporary concurrency cap increase and cache warmup for hot prefixes.
- Filed INC-4721 for session-affinity regression; fix ETA for permanent affinity improvements: 48–72 hours.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- By 2026-03-31: deploy affinity fix and automated cache prefetching for FinServe’s top prefixes.
- By 2026-04-05: permanent routing policy update to reduce single-AZ blast radius and automated health-based failover thresholds.
- Commercial: Laura, can we align on a credit proposal based on tonight’s impact window? I’ll prepare the detailed timeline and cost impact; we can propose credits tied to observed revenue impact or a service credit per SLA.

Attachments: runbook_failover_steps.pdf, finserve_metrics_snapshot.png
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4721, https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-FinServe-logs

I’ll follow up with a full RCA document by tomorrow EOD. Markus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
